body:
FAILURE: InvalidCursorError — OrdariumError with code "INVALID_CURSOR" ("The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point").

Surface: Ordarium's state change feed (the "observation" surface) — StateStore.changes(filter?, cursor?) -> StateChangeFeed.changes -> SqliteLedger.changes(), in the pinned @ordarium/core + @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1. The "stored observation cursor" is StateChangePage.cursor: per types.d.ts it is the always-present, "opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change" that a consumer persists and resumes from ("durable ledger commit-observation order").

Triggers, both fail-closed with InvalidCursorError:
1. Decode failure: cursor is not base64url of JSON, payload is not an object, `c` is not all-digits, or the decoded value is not a non-negative safe integer (decodeStateChangeCursor in core ledger.js and ledger-sqlite index.js).
2. Semantic rejection: decoded position > the ledger-wide high-water mark `SELECT MAX(change_seq) FROM ordarium_state_changes`. The cursor is global/filter-independent — compared against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence. Concurrent commits only raise the mark (so an honest cursor cannot be falsely rejected); a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and rejects.

What it is NOT (this is the decision the errors.d.ts comment makes explicit):
- Not LedgerCorruptError / "LEDGER_CORRUPT": InvalidCursorError is invalid caller input, not damaged ledger content.
- Not "LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED": SqliteLedger declares capabilities.stateChangeFeed = true, so the capability gate passes.
- Not the busy/transient families: it is neither isLedgerBusyError (LedgerBusyError), isTransientOperationError (Uncertain/Busy/SimulatedCrash), nor isStateRevisionConflict (StateRevisionConflictError). Retrying with the same stored cursor is futile; the integration must treat the stored position as unresumable, discard it, and re-establish from a fresh full read (or reconcile out-of-band) — never silently restart from position 0 (that is exactly what fail-closed refuses to do).

CONFLICT RESOLUTION (why no peer escalation): 09-error-contract-a.md (global) and 09-error-contract-b.md (per-consumer) each claim "normative, current scope" and contradict directly. They are not co-authoritative: (a) neither appears in docs/engineering/README.md (the 09 slot is 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md), and neither is referenced anywhere else in the workspace; (b) the change-feed contract is Ordarium-owned (07-ordarium-alignment.md §0/§1.3: Palimpsest consumes only public Ordarium contracts; §3.2 #4: new codes are mapped by instanceof, never hard-coded); (c) version scope is single — package.json, pnpm-workspace overrides and the installed packages all pin 1.3.1, and the pinned source is internally consistent across MemoryLedger and SqliteLedger. The pinned implementation is global/filter-independent, matching Record A and falsifying Record B. So the apparent A/B conflict is an unindexed documentation artifact, not a genuinely unresolved load-bearing conflict; local provenance analysis is sufficient and the peer (ordarium.main) need not be consulted.

Note on scope: Palimpsest does not yet consume changes() (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts uses list() pagination, whose malformed-cursor path throws TypeError, not InvalidCursorError). This is therefore the failure the integration should expect from the observation/change-feed surface if/when it stores a StateChangePage.cursor. Secondary observation: docs 07 (r18/r19) still describes a 1.2.0 four-line pin while the actual pin/install is 1.3.1 — a doc-lag to fix on the next commit; it does not change the contract above (the global-high-water behavior is unchanged).

Cannot legitimately determine yet: the load-bearing proposition is split across two competing normative sources on a peer-owned (Ordarium) contract boundary, and no accepted authority-participation basis exists.

DETERMINABLE BEHAVIOR (evidence, but not the contract authority):
When a stored observation cursor is rejected, the integration should expect InvalidCursorError — OrdariumError with code "INVALID_CURSOR", "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point".
- Surface: the state change feed (StateStore.changes / StateChangeFeed.changes). The stored cursor is StateChangePage.cursor — types.d.ts calls it the always-present "opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change" ("durable ledger commit-observation order").
- Rejection triggers: (1) undecodable cursor (bad base64url/JSON, non-digit c, non-safe-integer/negative) via decodeStateChangeCursor; (2) decoded position > the ledger-wide high-water mark (SqliteLedger: SELECT MAX(change_seq) FROM ordarium_state_changes; MemoryLedger: #stateChanges.length).
- It is explicitly not LedgerCorruptError/"LEDGER_CORRUPT" (errors.js: invalid caller input, not damaged ledger content) and not "LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED" (SqliteLedger declares stateChangeFeed=true). It fails closed instead of silently restarting at position 0, and it is not in the busy (LEDGER_BUSY), transient (OPERATION_UNCERTAIN/BUSY, SIMULATED_PROCESS_CRASH), or STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT families — so same-cursor retry is not a recovery; the stored position must be discarded and re-established from a fresh read.
- Pinned line: @ordarium/core and @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 (package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, installed packages agree).

WHY THIS IS NOT RESOLVED:
docs/engineering/09-error-contract-a.md ("global — one position shared by all readers") and docs/engineering/09-error-contract-b.md ("per-consumer — each consumer holds its own independent position") both declare themselves "normative, current scope" and directly contradict. They cannot both govern. Local provenance analysis does not break the tie (no dates, no explicit supersession, neither is listed in docs/engineering/README.md — the 09 slot there is 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md — and neither is referenced anywhere else). The state change-feed cursor contract is Ordarium-owned (docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md §0/§1.3: consume only public Ordarium contracts; §3.2 #4: map new codes by instanceof, not numeric code), so the pinned implementation is evidence of behavior, not the authority that selects the surviving normative record. My earlier resolved attempt was correctly blocked with UNRESOLVED_LOAD_BEARING_AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY.

AUTHORITY SOUGHT (no response yet):
- Thread thr_d8d897d9-7cd0-4106-bd84-804c22b9538e: question evt_e0a35ce1-04dd-4f1f-8250-ddbed3cbac92, proposal evt_6cbd963b-155f-4138-82e8-d622c20ffe55.
- Thread thr_6e2702bc-6a71-45d7-8132-1ad1a47571dd: need evt_7cc1698d-a38b-4b39-94b0-a699bea7c1a3.
- BoundaryContract ordarium-change-feed-cursor-contract revision 2 (termsDigest 9bce2143cfa646c49c670f5623a3f8052666b6b630e9e73d69be75ba1ebd2bad): status still "draft"; acceptedBy contains only palimpsest.main, no ordarium.main acceptance. collab_inbox delivered no events.

RESUME CONDITION: ordarium.main accepts that revision (or proposes a corrected one naming which of Record A / Record B is withdrawn/superseded). Then the determination is: failure = InvalidCursorError / INVALID_CURSOR on a global, ledger-wide, filter-independent observation position; rejection is unresumable; it is not LEDGER_CORRUPT, not busy, not transient; the surviving internal record is whichever the accepted terms match.
